title: The higher-precedence item's CALCULATE surrounds the lower item's whole expression: DIVIDE runs inside ALL ( T )
query: EVALUATE ROW ( "r", CALCULATE ( [Total], T[Item] = "A", Spread[Spread] = "All Rows", Per[Per] = "Per Row" ) )

source.supports: with YTD (precedence 20) above Daily Average (10), the combined expression is the lower item inside the higher item's CALCULATE, not DIVIDE(CALCULATE(SELECTEDMEASURE(), DATESYTD(DimDate[Date])), COUNTROWS(DimDate))

source.quote: The calculation group with the highest value is applied first; then the other calculation groups are applied according to their Precedence value in a descending order.

derivation: Spread first: CALCULATE ( SELECTEDMEASURE (), ALL ( T ) ), then Per inside it: CALCULATE ( DIVIDE ( [Total], COUNTROWS ( T ) ), ALL ( T ) ) = 60 / 3 = 20 (a double: DIVIDE). The other nesting, DIVIDE ( CALCULATE ( [Total], ALL ( T ) ), COUNTROWS ( T ) ) under T[Item] = "A", would give 60 / 1 = 60.
